skill.description: Reviews C# and .NET code against Microsoft naming conventions, async patterns, exception handling, LINQ usage, and modern C# style. Helps generate refactors and review feedback using documented examples.
skill.summary: Review and improve C# and .NET code using modern Microsoft conventions.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline C# identifiers, and documentation headings. The skill is documentation-only and guides .NET code review for naming, async patterns, exceptions, LINQ, and modern C# style. No prompt injection, command execution, network access, credential handling, or data exfiltration intent was found.

content.user_title: Review .NET Code for Modern C# Practices
content.value_statement: C# teams need consistent reviews for naming, async flow, exceptions, and LINQ usage. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused checklist with concrete .NET examples.
actual_capabilities: Checks C# naming against PascalCase, camelCase, interface, enum, and async method rules.
Flags outdated type usage such as framework type names instead of language keywords.
Identifies async anti-patterns including async void, blocking waits, and missing Async suffixes.
Reviews exception handling for broad catches, empty catches, and disposable usage.
Suggests modern C# refactors such as records, target-typed new, and file-scoped namespaces.
Uses included examples to show before-and-after review guidance.
limitations: It is guidance, not a compiler or full static analyzer.
It depends on the code and project context provided by the user.
Project .editorconfig rules can override the default style guidance.
It focuses on style and maintainability, not deep security testing.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Review C# changes for naming, async flow, exception handling, and modern syntax before merge.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Code Style
use_cases.description: Apply one .NET convention checklist across services, DTOs, repositories, and library code.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Refactoring Sessions
use_cases.description: Give Claude Code or Codex specific .NET review rules before editing existing C# files.

prompt_templates.title: Basic C# Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C# file for naming conventions, language keyword usage, and clear method names. Return the most important improvements first.

prompt_templates.title: Async and Exception Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this .NET service for async anti-patterns, exception handling issues, and disposable usage. Explain each finding with a practical fix.

prompt_templates.title: Modern C# Refactor Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Find opportunities to use records, file-scoped namespaces, target-typed new, collection expressions, and cleaner LINQ in this codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Full Pull Request Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these C# changes as a pull request. Prioritize behavioral risks, maintainability issues, style violations, and missing tests.

output_examples.input: A service method uses async void and catches the base exception type.
output_examples.output: The review flags async void as unsafe outside event handlers and recommends returning a task. It also recommends catching specific exceptions.

output_examples.input: A DTO class contains mutable properties and manual equality methods.
output_examples.output: The review suggests a record when immutability fits the design. It explains how this reduces boilerplate and improves intent.

output_examples.input: A pull request mixes framework type names, block namespaces, and repeated enumeration.
output_examples.output: The review groups style fixes separately from performance concerns. It recommends language keywords, file-scoped namespaces, and materializing the sequence once.

best_practices: Provide the relevant .editorconfig file before asking for style feedback.
Ask for prioritized findings when reviewing large pull requests.
Separate style modernization from behavior changes during refactoring.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad rewrites without sharing tests or expected behavior.
Do not apply generic conventions when the project has explicit local rules.
Do not treat style suggestions as proof that compiled behavior is correct.

faq.question: Does this skill compile or run .NET code?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and refactoring suggestions based on the supplied files.

faq.question: Can it follow my project style rules?
faq.answer: Yes, if you provide the .editorconfig file or explain the local conventions.

faq.question: What C# versions does it target?
faq.answer: It emphasizes modern C# patterns, especially C# 10 and newer guidance.

faq.question: Is this mainly for code review or generation?
faq.answer: It supports both, but its strongest use is structured review and focused refactoring.

faq.question: Does it cover security review?
faq.answer: Only at a basic code-quality level. Use a dedicated security review for vulnerability analysis.

faq.question: Can Claude Code and Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is Markdown guidance that can steer Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
